## What is biostatistics?

Biostatistics is a sister field to statistics that focuses on data about human health. Biostatisticians:

- analyze data
- design and analyze clinical and population studies in biomedical research
- develop and validate new methods and tools
- communicate results to scientific and general audiences

You don't need a science background, just curiosity. Some biology helps but is not required.

## How you'll learn

The curriculum follows the full cycle of study design and data analysis:

**ask a question → explore the data → model it → communicate the findings**.

:::::: grid
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
**Scientific context**<br>A public health core, plus electives across the health sciences.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
**Programming and visualization**<br>R and SAS, with reproducible data analysis.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
**Modeling uncertainty**<br>Biostatistics core courses, plus electives in epidemiology, statistics and computer science.
:::
::::::

## What the program looks like

::::::: facts
::: fact
[17 credits]{.num} [**Biostats core**: methods, data science, advanced R and specialized electives]{.label}
:::

::: fact
[6 credits]{.num} [**Culminating experience**: a project course plus an elective, or a thesis]{.label}
:::

::: fact
[4 credits]{.num} [**Electives**: biostatistics, statistics, epidemiology, computer science and more]{.label}
:::

::: fact
[3 credits]{.num} [**Public health core**]{.label}
:::
:::::::

Students without prior statistics coursework also take **0–7 credits of biostats foundation courses** (regression, probability and inference, computing with R).

| Component | Credits | What it covers |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Biostats foundation** | 0–7 | Regression, probability and inference, and computing with R. Math/stat majors with prior coursework can waive these. |
| **Public health core** | 3 | Includes a 1-credit public health class. |
| **Biostats core** | 17 | Topics in biostatistics, data science and epidemiology; advanced R; specialized electives such as survival analysis, Bayesian statistics and clinical trials. |
| **Electives** | 4 | Biostatistics, statistics, epidemiology, computer science and more. |
| **Culminating experience** | 6 | A project-based course (3) plus one elective (3), *or* an MS thesis (6). |

: A course is usually 3 credits.

### How long does it take?

- **With a math or statistics background:** about 3 semesters, or 2 semesters plus a summer (30 credits).
- **Without prior statistics:** about 4 semesters (30–37 credits, including the foundation courses).

## Culminating experience

You finish the program by bringing your training together in one of two ways.

### Project course: Biostatistics in Action (BIOSTATS 690E)

This is where your biostatistics and public health education all comes together. You work on a real-world public health problem as a biostatistician: you develop your own research protocol (literature review, study design, statistical analysis plan, and power and sample size calculation), carry out the analysis, write a manuscript and present your findings. Taught by [Alex Knee](https://www.umass.edu/public-health-sciences/about/directory/alex-knee), an applied biostatistician and epidemiologist with 20 years of experience at an academic medical center. [More on the course →](courses.qmd)

Examples of capstone projects:

- **A Difference-in-Differences Analysis of State Medicaid Expansion and Cost-Related Delay of Care.** Cole Spinale (MS 2026)

- **Comparing Multivariable Prediction Models to Classify Current Smoking Status Among U.S. Adults Using Demographic and Socioeconomic Characteristics.** Jordyn Sullivan (MS 2026)

### MS thesis

Alternatively, you can do a 6-credit MS thesis, working one-on-one with a faculty advisor on an original research project.

Examples of MS theses:

- **Public masking mandates and COVID-19 growth rates.** Angus Wong (MS 2021); published in *Epidemiology* (2022).
- **Bayesian spatial models of birth weight in Ghana.** Barbara Mottey (MS 2021).
- **Spatio-temporal clusters of SARS-CoV-2 infections.** Keith Allison (MS 2022).
- **Estimating the Change in Expected All-Cause ED Hospitalizations During the COVID-19 Pandemic in Massachusetts.** Amani Chehimi (MS 2025).
- **Statistical Methods for Regression Analysis with Interval-censored Covariates.** Lin Cai (MS 2026).

## The 4+1 MS

Undergraduates at UMass and the Five Colleges can start the MS in their senior year and finish in one extra year. [Learn about the 4+1 →](4plus1.qmd)
